contracts.name: MidwayBuyer
contracts.notice: Stable application-facing contract that routes each request to its saved Engine.

functions.notice: Accepts FWA's token bid for the recorded application account.
Activates staged FWA listings before quoting.

Claims closed-epoch purchaser rewards. Restricted to the request's recorded account: the rewards land on `purchaserRewardRecipient` either way, so a third-party claim consumes the epoch out of band and strips whatever attribution the account performs around its own claim.

Extension hatch (D17 Option A). Forwards `data` to the request's pinned engine via `onExtensionCall`, appending `msg.sender` as a trailing 20 bytes so the engine can authorize per payload selector without trusting a caller-supplied argument. FwaEngineV1 reverts unconditionally; this is dead code until a future engine version implements a payload.
Non-request-scoped counterpart of `extensionCall`, forwarded to `activeEngine`. Gated to registered, active application accounts, the same check `_acquire` applies.
Recovers ETH mis-sent to the router. Sends the full balance: the router never holds ETH as part of an acquisition, so any balance here is stray.
Recovers an ERC721 mis-sent to the router.
Recovers an ERC20 mis-sent to the router. The router holds no protocol funds itself; every acquisition's ETH and reward flow routes through the engine, request buyer, and reward vault instead.

Acquire-pacing signals from the active engine's FWA pool, the single Midway-side read a keeper consults before requesting a new acquisition. See `FwaEngineV1.acquisitionReadiness`: a nonzero `unfulfilledVrf` means FWA's VRF subscription is under pressure and a further acquire may revert `InsufficientVrfCoverage`, so the keeper should `processAcquisitions` and wait for fulfillment rather than firing into it.

contracts.name: MidwayRegistry
contracts.notice: Registers applications and their authorized purchasing accounts.

functions.notice: Point the engines at a FWAT conversion-floor policy contract (`floorId()` must be `MIDWAY_FWA_CONVERSION_FLOOR_V1`). Zero clears it, after which every engine-driven FWAT buy is refused until a policy is set again.
Sets the default for future managed requests. Existing requests keep their snapshot.
The FWAT conversion-floor policy every engine reads for its minimum output on accrued-reward claims and managed FWAT settlement. Operator-replaceable.

contracts.name: FwaEngineV1
contracts.notice: Immutable integration for the deployed FWA v1 surface.

functions.notice: Accepts FWA's token bid using the account-supplied minimum output.

Extension hatch receiving hook (D17 Option A), forwarded from MidwayBuyer.extensionCall. V1 ships no extension verbs: this reverts before any state read, so no funds path exists through it. A future engine version decodes `data` against its own versioned selector table and authorizes using the original external caller, which MidwayBuyer appends as a trailing 20 bytes of calldata after the abi-encoded call. Dead code at launch; flagged for the external audit.
Non-request-scoped counterpart of `onExtensionCall`, forwarded from MidwayBuyer.extensionCallGlobal. Same launch behavior: unconditional revert before any state read.

Minimum token output for an accrued-reward claim on `midwayRequestId`: the request's unspent FWARewards allowance and the conversion-floor policy on it. `valid` is false when the allowance is zero or no effective floor exists; `claimAccruedRewards` reverts in either case.

Acquire-pacing signals read from FWA, for a keeper to gate a new acquisition rather than firing one into FWA's VRF backpressure. FWA reverts `InsufficientVrfCoverage` when its subscription cannot underwrite another callback while `unfulfilledVrf` requests are outstanding; a keeper seeing a nonzero `unfulfilledVrf` should call `processAcquisitions` and wait for fulfillment before requesting. `priced` is false when the pool cannot currently quote (also unacquirable), and `activeListings` is zero when nothing is selectable. A pure read: it never predicts coverage exactly (that lives in FWA's VRF service), it surfaces the signals the caller paces on.
Calculates the FWA fee cap represented by a Midway acquisition fee cap.
Whether the request can be resolved permissionlessly.
Minimum token output for a managed FWAT settlement paying `ethPayout`: the registry's conversion-floor policy on it, or invalid below `minimumManagedFwaPayout`.
Splits funding into the FWA budget and Midway fee reserve.

contracts.name: RequestBuyer
contracts.notice: Single-use FWA purchaser for one Midway request.

functions.notice: Settles through FWA's token bid and sends the measured output to RewardVault.

Spends this request's accrued surcharge allowance on FWARewards' token buy and forwards the output to the RewardVault. The engine derives `minOut` from the effective conversion floor (`FwaEngineV1.accruedRewardMinimumOutput`); a zero bound is refused here so no caller can route an unbounded buy through this clone.
Credits referral rewards without making settlement depend on the recipient.

contracts.notice: Live collection delivery policy used by immutable Engine versions.

contracts.name: RewardVault
contracts.notice: FWAT custody with measured ingress and address-owned pots.

functions.notice: Credit FWAT held by this vault above `totalAttributed` to `pot`. Surplus accumulates from raw transfers into the vault that never went through `deposit`. Owner only.

functions.dev: Compatibility read for older Registry integrations. A nonzero pot address is valid; RewardVault intentionally has no controller allowlist.

contracts.name: RewardSplitter
contracts.notice: Splits purchaser rewards three ways: treasury, shared upside, and the application. All shares stay in RewardVault custody as pot attributions: the recipient pulls its own pot whenever it chooses (`RewardVault.transfer`) or migrates it onward, so delivery imposes no requirement on the recipient beyond pot ownership.

functions.notice: Set the treasury and shared-upside shares together, so the pair stays consistent. Registry operator only; bounded by `MAX_TREASURY_BPS` and `MAX_SKIM_BPS`.
Set the treasury pot address. Registry operator only; nonzero.
Ceiling on the shared-upside share, a fat-finger guard on an economic lever.
Ceiling on the treasury share, a fat-finger guard on an economic lever.
Shared-upside share of gross rewards, in bps. Set at construction; mutable by the registry operator afterward via `setSplit`. Applies to `split` calls after the change, never retroactively.

Treasury pot address in RewardVault. Mutable by the registry operator; applies to `split` calls after the change. FWAT already attributed to the prior address stays in that pot; moving it onward is the prior treasury's own call.
Treasury share of gross rewards, in bps. Set at construction; mutable by the registry operator afterward via `setSplit`. Applies to `split` calls after the change, never retroactively.

Give up on a pending cycle's randomness: clears the pending slot, returns the reserved pot to `drawablePot()`, and marks the cycle `Abandoned`. The cycle's first randomness request must be at least `cycle.vrfRetryDelay` old for either caller; a non-owner additionally waits until `ABANDON_AFTER` has elapsed past the cycle's end.
functions.dev: The recovery for a subscription that was deleted, drained, or dropped this contract as a consumer while a request was in flight. Without it `pendingCycleId` never clears, every later `checkpoint` reverts `PendingRandomness`, and the reserved pot is stranded. A callback that arrives afterward is rejected by `fulfillRandomness`'s `pendingCycleId != cycleId` check, so the pot cannot be paid twice.Both legs are anchored on values no caller can move: `firstRequestedAt` is written once and `cycleEnd` is fixed. `requestedAt` is not usable here because `retryRandomness` is permissionless and rewrites it, so a gate keyed to it can be held shut by one retry per `vrfRetryDelay`.

functions.notice: Time after a cycle ends before `abandonPendingCycle` opens to anyone. Seven days is `_validateConfig`'s ceiling on `vrfRetryDelay`, so at least one full retry interval fits inside it under every valid configuration. Measured from `cycleEnd`, which is fixed: `cycle.requestedAt` moves on every `retryRandomness`, and that call is permissionless, so a deadline keyed to it could be pushed back indefinitely.

Time after a cycle ends before `checkpoint` will skip it for an empty `drawablePot()`. Inside the grace period the call reverts `EmptyDrawablePot` instead, so a checkpoint landing in the gap between the cycle's end and the PrizeReserve's conversion cannot burn the cycle's draw. One day, well inside the shortest supported funding cadence and short enough that a genuinely unfunded cycle still clears the cursor promptly.
Maximum number of VRF requests for one cycle, including the initial request.

events.notice: A pending cycle's randomness was given up on. The reserved pot returns to `drawablePot()` and a late callback for this cycle is rejected.
A cycle whose gate passed was skipped without a draw because `drawablePot()` was zero at checkpoint. No pot was reserved and the checkpoint cursor advanced.

contracts.name: ReferralRewards
contracts.notice: Pull-credit sink for referral ETH earned from terminal Midway fees.

functions.notice: Pays a referrer's entire pull credit. Anyone may call this function.

RequestBuyer ingress: the caller is the one-request buyer, while `engine` is its immutable authority. This lets deployments approve immutable Engines without enumerating every deterministic RequestBuyer clone.

contracts.name: FwaConversionFloor
contracts.notice: Minimum-output policy for every FWAT buy the Midway engine drives (accrued-reward claims, managed FWAT settlement). Registered on MidwayRegistry as `conversionFloor` and replaceable by the registry operator; the engine reads it at call time. The effective floor for a buy of `ethIn` is the strictest of four legs: - observation: expected output at the best (highest FWAT per ETH) pool price among the recorded observations that are usable, after the 1% hook fee, less `slippageCapBps`. An observation is usable when it was recorded in an earlier block and is at most `observationWindowBlocks` old. Fewer than `minObservations` usable observations make the floor invalid and the engine refuses the buy; - spot: the same quote at the pool's current `sqrtPriceX96`, less `slippageCapBps`; - FWA: FWAToken's own `buybackSqrtPriceLimitX96` when armed (the min-sqrt sentinel and any invalid read count as no FWA floor); - absolute: `floorRate` FWAT per ETH when nonzero. The result must clear `MIN_FLOOR_RATE` on `ethIn` or it is invalid. The pool exposes no oracle. `recordObservation` is permissionless and stores the live spot in the ring slot of the current bucket (`observationWindowBlocks / OBSERVATION_SLOTS` blocks per bucket); within a bucket the highest FWAT per ETH price is kept, so a recorded observation is replaced only by a stricter one and ages out with its bucket. A pushed price reaches the floor only when every usable observation is at a pushed price, which needs the pool held at that price across `minObservations` buckets: from `bucketBlocks * (minObservations - 2) + 2` blocks when the ring is empty (18 at launch) up to the whole window when honest observations are present. Sells through the pool are open to every FWAT holder, so a held push is exposed to holders selling into it; the holder set is small because FWAT is otherwise transfer locked. The cost is one round trip of the hook fee on the pushed amount plus that capital held, so the floor removes the same-block sandwich, not a held one. An observation recorded at a price above the current one makes the floor stricter than the pool can pay until its bucket ages out of the window.

functions.notice: Store the pool's current `sqrtPriceX96` as the observation of the current bucket. Anyone may call. When the bucket already holds an observation, the call succeeds only with a higher FWAT per ETH price; otherwise it reverts `ObservationNotImproved`. Reverts when the pool cannot be read. The observation becomes usable in the next block.
Set the absolute floor. Zero disables it; any other value must be at least `MIN_FLOOR_RATE`.
Set the usable observations required for a valid floor. Zero disables the observation leg; any other value is at most `OBSERVATION_SLOTS`.

Set the observation window. At least `OBSERVATION_SLOTS` and at most `MAX_OBSERVATION_WINDOW_BLOCKS`. Bucket boundaries move with the window: stored observations keep their block, age out on the new window, and a stored observation whose block no longer maps to the current bucket of its slot is replaced by the next record in that slot at any price.
Set the slippage cap. At most `MAX_SLIPPAGE_CAP_BPS`.
The observation stored for the current bucket, if any. `recorded` is false when the bucket's ring slot is empty or holds an observation from an earlier bucket.
Optional absolute floor in FWAT per ETH scaled by 1e18. Zero disables it.
Upper bound on `observationWindowBlocks` (about one day).
Upper bound on `slippageCapBps`: a spot-relative leg never sits more than 10% under its reference price.

Lowest nonzero `floorRate` accepted, and the dust bound every effective floor must clear: 1e15 = 0.001 FWAT per ETH. A weaker bound reads as configured while permitting a buy at effectively any output.

Uniswap v3 MIN_SQRT_PRICE + 1. FWAToken carries this as `buybackSqrtPriceLimitX96` when its buyback has no price limit; it derives a zero output floor at any realistic scale, so it is read as no FWA floor rather than a floor of zero.

The effective minimum output for a buy of `ethIn`. `valid` is false when fewer than `minObservations` observations are usable, when no leg exists, or when the combined floor is below `MIN_FLOOR_RATE` on `ethIn`. `fwaSqrtPriceLimitX96` is FWAToken's raw limit when it is a usable floor, else zero.
Usable observations required for a valid floor. Zero disables the observation leg.
Observation ring size, and the upper bound on `minObservations`.
The stored observation at ring index `index` (0 to `OBSERVATION_SLOTS` - 1).
Age in blocks past which an observation is not usable. At least `OBSERVATION_SLOTS` so every ring slot maps to a bucket of at least one block.
Slippage cap in bps applied to the observation and spot legs. Zero disables the spot leg and makes the observation leg exact.

The pool's current `sqrtPriceX96` and the expected FWAT output for `ethIn` at that price after the 1% hook fee, before the slippage cap. `valid` is false when the PoolManager read fails or the pool is uninitialized.
The usable observations right now and the best (highest FWAT per ETH) `sqrtPriceX96` among them. `bestSqrtPriceX96` is zero when none is usable.
